short_description: Mental health EHR with integrated insurance billing, ERA auto-posting, and eligibility verification at competitive per-claim pricing.
long_description: TherapyNotes Billing provides mental health professionals with streamlined insurance claims submission integrated directly into their practice management workflow. Founded in 2010 by a licensed psychologist, the platform was built specifically for behavioral health practices. The billing module includes electronic claims submission through Apex EDI clearinghouse, real-time eligibility verification, electronic remittance advice (ERA) auto-posting, and patient billing capabilities. TherapyNotes uses proprietary 'wisp' note templates that automatically suggest appropriate CPT codes based on session content. The system supports professional claims (CMS-1500), handles secondary insurance billing, and provides claim tracking with denial management. With one of the lowest per-claim fees in the industry at $0.14 per claim, TherapyNotes offers excellent value for practices submitting moderate claim volumes.

faqs.q: How much does TherapyNotes charge per insurance claim?
faqs.a: TherapyNotes charges $0.14 per electronic claim submission, which is one of the lowest rates in the mental health practice management market. Eligibility verifications cost an additional $0.03 each. There are no hidden fees or percentages of collections taken.

Yes, TherapyNotes includes electronic remittance advice (ERA) enrollment and auto-posting at no additional cost. Once enrolled with payers for ERAs, payments are automatically applied to patient accounts, significantly reducing manual posting time and errors.

TherapyNotes uses Apex EDI as their clearinghouse partner for electronic claims submission. Apex connects to thousands of payers nationwide including all major commercial insurers, Medicare, and Medicaid programs.

faqs.q: Can TherapyNotes handle telehealth billing with proper modifiers?
faqs.a: Yes, TherapyNotes fully supports telehealth billing with appropriate place of service codes (typically 02 or 10) and modifiers (95, GT, etc.). The system automatically applies telehealth settings when sessions are marked as video appointments and maintains compliance with payer-specific telehealth billing requirements.
